calls.head: Calgary should get plenty of shots away
calls.body: Seattle is 30th of 32 at shot suppression, and Calgary is one of the league’s busiest shooting teams (5th: 62.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5).
calls.call: Calgary takes at least its usual 62.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Calgary took 73.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 62.5.

calls.head: Seattle pounces on mistakes, and Calgary makes them
calls.body: Seattle ranks 10th of 32 for chances off turnovers (7.5% of its chances come right after winning the puck); Calgary ranks 30th for avoiding breakdowns.
calls.call: At least its usual 7.5% of Seattle’s 5-on-5 chances come right after winning the puck.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 6.5% of Seattle’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.5%.

SEA.head: We had this close to even (57% for Seattle), and Seattle came through.

CGY.head: We had this close to even (43% for Calgary), and it went Seattle’s way.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Wolf
surprises.body: D. Wolf allowed 6 goals on shots worth 2.7 expected goals, 3.3 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 50 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Seattle tried a different line
surprises.body: J. McCann, M. Beniers, M. Samoskevich played 13:21 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Seattle’s usual lines.
